attempts.error: The encrypted volume could not be created. Node1 entered a kernel networking deadlock that blocked package installation, then failed to regain command access after an acknowledged native reboot. No storage or boot configuration was modified.

diagnosis.summary: Attempt 1 was correctly blocked: no encrypted volume was created and the boot-persistence requirement was not tested. The evidence proves that cryptsetup was absent, several DNF processes and kernel workers were stuck in uninterruptible networking/RTNL-related waits, and command access was lost after a reboot was scheduled. It does not prove a kernel deadlock, that the reboot completed, or why the node never became reachable again.

evidence.finding: Node1 ran CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. Its only disk was /dev/vda; /dev/vda3 contained the XFS root filesystem with about 19 GiB free. There was no spare block device, /srv/secure, backing image, key file, crypttab entry, or fstab entry.
The cryptsetup package and cryptsetup CLI were absent, although cryptsetup-libs, device-mapper components, and systemd-cryptsetup were installed.

Multiple DNF processes were in D state at rtnl_dumpit, and networking-related kernel workers were also in D state. This establishes a persistent RTNL/networking-path stall that prevented the attempted package installation; it does not establish the underlying defect or prove a permanent deadlock.

systemd accepted and started a transient service invoking systemctl reboot. The last successful checks still showed the original boot ID; later checks returned an origin error or connection resets. Therefore reboot completion and a new boot identity were not observed.
No evidence shows any storage or boot configuration was changed, and there is no evidence that /srv/secure was ever encrypted, mounted, or verified across a reboot.

likely_causes.cause: A pre-existing kernel networking/RTNL stall blocked DNF and related network queries.
The stall was a true kernel deadlock rather than a prolonged lock contention or another kernel/network subsystem failure.
Shutdown or reboot became stuck because of the same kernel condition.
The node rebooted successfully but its management transport failed to recover.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh node, immediately capture OS, kernel, boot ID, lsblk, free space, and existing crypttab/fstab state; keep the installed release and kernel unchanged.

Before starting package work, use short timeouts to test an RTNL query and DNF responsiveness. Avoid launching concurrent DNF health checks and installation commands. If the same stall is already present, stop early and report it rather than accumulating blocked processes.
Install the distribution-provided cryptsetup package while the fresh node is responsive. Confirm the executable and package version before modifying storage.

Because the specified layout has no spare disk, use a sensibly sized file-backed LUKS container on the root filesystem, create an XFS filesystem inside its mapper device, and mount it at /srv/secure. Check free space before allocating it.

Create a root-only key file under /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d, reference the backing file and key in /etc/crypttab, and reference the mapper device in /etc/fstab. A local key enables unattended boot but provides weaker protection if an attacker obtains the root disk and key together.
Before rebooting, validate crypttab/fstab syntax, reload systemd, activate and mount the volume, and verify findmnt, cryptsetup status, permissions, and a write/read test.

Perform one native reboot only after the live configuration works. Prove success with a changed boot ID plus findmnt /srv/secure, cryptsetup status, filesystem type, and a post-boot write/read test. Do not claim reboot persistence from connection loss alone.
